## Highlights

- From-scratch tile-based Gaussian-splatting rasteriser in PyTorch with a **hand-derived backward
  pass** (means, scale/rotation, opacity, SH degree 0-3, rendered depth), checked against autograd
  and finite differences
- Online mapping from insight-vio poses: keyframes, silhouette growth from depth, sliding window,
  clone/split/prune, per-splat Adam
- Synthetic lab walk (36 s, measured on a desktop CPU, 2026-11-26): 49,460 splats, insight-vio ATE
  4.2 cm, held-out PSNR 27.6 dB from the VIO pose / 21.0 dB from the true pose; 31.3 dB with
  ground-truth poses (ablation)
- Live-stream protocol v1 over WebSocket (ADD / UPDATE / REMOVE / FRAME / RESET), delta encoder,
  hand-written RFC 6455 server and `.sslog` replay; splatweb `feat/live-stream` renders it in place

## Downloads

- `splatscan-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`, `splatscan-0.1.0.tar.gz`: the Python package
  (`pip install` also pulls insight-vio from GitHub)
- `splatscan-protocol-v1-fixture.tar.gz`: a small reference stream + expected decoded state, for
  writing other clients

## Not yet verified

- Anything on a Jetson: `deploy/jetson/` config and systemd unit, `splatscan/hw.py` camera/IMU wiring
- Real cameras, the lab-walk video, Vanta integration
- Real-time operation: mapping took 1.38 s per iteration on the (heavily shared) desktop CPU and
  0.30 s on an RTX 2060 through PyTorch CUDA
